title: The Footprints by the Pond
synopsis: Pip and Moss make guesses about marks beside a pond, then watch a small duck drag a twig through the mud.

related_resources.reason: Strategies for inviting inquiry, not a controlled trial of this fictional story.
Examples of adult-supported observation and experimentation; not proof that one narrative changes reasoning skills.
Population developmental milestones and caregiver prompts; not proof that fiction produces an outcome and not an individual diagnostic rule.

rationale_citations.story_anchor: Pip wasn't sure. The marks looked so small.
rationale_citations.editorial_rationale: A guess can remain provisional while more is observed.
rationale_citations.evidence_scope: Open-ended inquiry supports the editorial choice; wildlife details are invented.

rationale_citations.story_anchor: A quiet splashing sound came from behind the reeds.
rationale_citations.editorial_rationale: The characters delay their conclusion until a further observation is available.
rationale_citations.evidence_scope: Guidance supports noticing and discussing observations; no measured outcome.

rationale_citations.editorial_rationale: Changing an explanation can be part of solving a playful mystery.
rationale_citations.evidence_scope: Not evidence of a child learning formal scientific reasoning.

source_note: The manuscript is original fictional narrative. Citations apply only to stated parent-facing developmental rationales; they do not source plots or establish an effect from listening to this story.
